PC: Assess and manage the patient’s airway by verifying patency, evaluating the presence and effort of breathing, and initiating appropriate oxygen supplementation as needed (via nasal cannula, facemask, high-flow nasal cannula, CPAP or BiPAP)
Establish IV access; if peripheral IV cannot be established rapidly then intraosseous access must be obtained
Assess patient for the presence of a pulse when there is an acute clinical change (patient will stop moaning)
Recognize the presence of pulseless ventricular tachycardia and employ PALS Pediatric Cardiac Arrest Algorithm by immediately beginning high quality CPR with synchronous BVM ventilation
Administer initial shock energy for defibrillation at 2J/kg and resume high quality CPR immediately after shock delivery
After 2 minutes with no change or improvement, administer second round of shock energy for defibrillation at 4J/kg and resume high quality CPR immediately after shock delivery
After second shock administer Epinephrine (1:10,000) 0.01mg/kg IV
Repeat defibrillation at >4J/kg (maximum of 10J/kg) every 2 minutes; repeat administration of Epinephrine every 3-5 minutes
MK: Connect patient to cardiopulmonary monitor (if not on monitor already) and correctly identify the presence of ventricular tachycardia (patient will initially be moaning and will have a pulse)
ICS: Anticipate the progression of ventricular tachycardia with a pulse to ventricular tachycardia without a pulse (i.e., request for defibrillator, assignment of CPR roles/responsibilities)
